title: array length is computed by the executable Flow before its durable timer is scheduled

xfail.reason: The Go backend still treats the timer duration as a legacy Plan projection and refuses array length. The JS executable body computes the duration, persists its absolute wake time, and replays without rescheduling. This records missing executable-body support, not permission to weaken the Flow contract.
xfail.doc: specification/durable-execution.mdx §Flow (SA-2): durable(...) MUST NOT change what the function computes; ordinary control flow and captures execute unchanged. The timer duration is computed before the checked persistence boundary.

notes:
specification/durable-execution.mdx §Flow (SA-2): 'durable(...) MUST NOT change what the function computes'. RETIRED 2026-09-06 by the implementation lane: the executable timer driver replaces the legacy Plan-only projection wall. The authored source is unchanged. poc/src/durable/body-timer.test.ts compiles this exact file, executes its two-item input through a signed deployment, observes durationMs: 2, and replays both the timer and Action with only one worker invocation. Separate tests prove lease-free scheduling, stable wake time across real SIGKILL/restart, cancellation, fencing and malformed-answer refusal. The corpus itself checks the descriptor marker, not durable execution. The earlier diagnostic rationale follows as implementation history, not a current language restriction.

specification/durable-execution.mdx:49 (Durable Boundary Contract): 'Every value crossing an Action or Flow persistence boundary MUST satisfy the compiler-checked durable codec contract', read with :71, 'Runtime-dependent control flow MUST be represented explicitly in Plan IR. The compiler MUST reject an operation that would inspect a symbolic value without a corresponding IR representation.' A timer's duration is a Plan value like any other and is subject to the same contract; a literal duration is already exercised, and must keep compiling, in 17-durable/static-plan-shape-is-digest-pinned. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS AND WHY IT IS NOT REDUNDANT WITH THE ACTION-INPUT ONE: the repair that closed this fail-open works by having every failure site drop its hard-coded "Flow output " prefix and letting the collecting walk prepend the subject of the value it is currently visiting. A case whose defect sits in an Action input cannot tell a subject that is chosen correctly from one hard-coded to "Action <id> input", and a case whose defect sits in the Flow output cannot tell it from one still hard-coded to "Flow output". This one can, because its subject is neither: the value is a timer duration, and the sentence has to say so. It is the case that catches a wrong subject. THE DECLARED POSITION: 10:29 is the `(` of the arrow function, not the `sleep` call and not the projection -- both implementations anchor this rule on the durable source function, because the descriptor that could not answer the path is the Flow's boundary contract rather than any one expression. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: five mutations run through both backends, each red on BOTH with the diff printed -- line 10 to 11, column 29 to 30, VIBE4110 to VIBE4111, `durable array` to `durable string`, and `sleep duration cannot project` to `Flow output cannot project`. That last one is the regression this case is FOR, and both backends print `sleep duration cannot project length from durable array` against it. The mutator refuses to run unless the case is green on both backends first AND its search string occurs exactly once in the file, and the file was restored and sha256-compared byte-identical after every one. NO MARKER on either backend: one diagnostic each, same code, line, column and sentence.
